{"type":"text","timestamp":1794627373777,"sessionID":"ses_e27e1d298ffelppXRTpARdfqeq","part":{"id":"prt_1d8208aca001KZ93EU8NtY6M5t","messageID":"msg_1d8206b69001QOLdoOISdi6kjK","sessionID":"ses_e27e1d298ffelppXRTpARdfqeq","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover sampled all five original targets on time and finished alive with 10 battery left. I couldn't check whether it ended inside the base radius: every position reading is noisy. The average of 15 stationary readings after the final drive is about (19.9, 19.6), roughly 0.4 m from base, which is inside the 0.75 m radius. If it did end at base, the score is 8 / 13 ≈ 0.62.\n\n- **Sampled (8 points):** t1, t5, t4 and t2 (2 + 2 + 1 + 2) and t3 (1), all before their deadlines.\n- **Missed d2 (3 points, deadline tick 22):** this was my mistake. I sent a drive command of 5.1 m, over the 5 m limit, so the whole batch was rejected. I didn't notice and let the clock run on, which lost two ticks. After that, d2 could only be sampled late, for 0.75 points, and later the battery was too low to take the detour.\n- **Missed d1 (2 points, deadline tick 28):** it was announced too late to reach by its deadline. Getting it late (0.5 points) would have needed about 15 battery and only about 13 was left, so going for it risked a flat battery and a score of zero.\n\nWhat worked: I planned routes along the edges of the sand where I could, because sand slip was uncertain. I sent each leg's commands ahead to keep the queue full despite the 3-tick delay.
